source_text:
Καὶ ἡμεῖς οὖν γενώμεθα ἐκ τῶν εὐχαριστούντων, δεδουλευκότων τῷ θεῷ, καὶ μὴ ἐκ τῶν κρινομένων ἀσεβῶν.
καὶ γὰρ αὐτὸς πανθαμαρτωλὸς ὢν καὶ μήπω φυγὼν τὸν πειρασμόν, ἀλλ’ ἔτι ὢν ἐν μέσοις τοῖς ὀργάνοις τοῦ διαβόλου σπουδάζω τὴν δικαιοσύνην διώκειν, ὅπως ἰσχύσω κἂν ἐγγὺς αὐτῆς γενέσθαι, φοβούμενος τὴν κρίσιν τὴν μέλλουσαν.
thought_title: The preacher includes himself among sinners who pursue righteousness
orientation: The preacher has just described the fate of the wicked and the hope of the righteous at the day of judgment, and now he turns to include himself and his hearers in the call to be among the thankful rather than the judged.
pass_a_gloss: And we therefore, let us become from among those who give thanks, who have served God, and not from among the wicked who are judged. For indeed I myself, being altogether sinful and not yet having fled the temptation, but still being in the midst of the instruments of the devil, I am eager to pursue righteousness, so that I may be strong enough at least to come near to it, fearing the judgment that is about to come.

choices.english: let us become from among those who give thanks
choices.why: The genitive with ἐκ marks the group from which the hearers are to take their identity; the hortatory subjunctive keeps the preacher's inclusive exhortation.
rejected: let us be among those who give thanks

choices.why: The perfect participle indicates completed service as a defining mark of the thankful group; the dative τῷ θεῷ is the object of service.
The compound adjective intensifies ἁμαρτωλός; the concessive participle ὢν is rendered with 'being' to preserve the participial force.
rejected: though I am a complete sinner

choices.why: ὄργανον here means the tools or devices by which the devil works; the plural suggests the various means of temptation.

choices.english: at least to come near to it
choices.why: κἄν (καὶ ἐάν) with the infinitive expresses the modest goal of even approaching righteousness; ἐγγύς with genitive means 'near to it.'
rejected: even to get close to it

choices.english: the judgment that is about to come
choices.why: The attributive participle μέλλουσαν with the article marks the judgment as future and impending; the repetition of the article is idiomatic Greek.

pass_b_english: So let us also take our place among those who give thanks, who have served God, and not among the wicked who are judged.

For I myself am altogether sinful. I have not yet escaped temptation, but I am still in the midst of the devil's instruments. Yet I am eager to pursue righteousness, so that I may at least have strength to come near to it, because I fear the judgment that is about to come.

last_rejected.why: πανθαμαρτωλός means 'worst of sinners' or 'utterly sinful,' but 'altogether sinful' understates the superlative force; more importantly, the English misses that this is a rare, emphatic compound.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Altogether sinful' fairly renders πανθαμαρτωλός; loss of compound's rarity is stylistic, not meaning-changing.

last_rejected.quote: have strength to come near to it
last_rejected.why: ἰσχύσω means 'be strong enough' or 'have the strength,' but the construction κἂν...γενέσθαι means 'even become near to it'—the Greek emphasizes attaining nearness, not just coming near.
last_rejected.fix: be strong enough even to become near to it
last_rejected.ruling: κἂν ἐγγὺς γενέσθαι = 'even come near'; 'have strength to come near' captures both ἰσχύσω and κἂν adequately.

polish.changed: Split the long second sentence into three shorter sentences so the speaker's confession, present struggle, and hope are easier to follow aloud.
